Question: What should be done when ABS says the delivery schedule will be two days short and the delivery date is not more than five days away?
Official Answer / SOP: When the delivery date is not more than five days away and ABS indicates that the case will be short by two days, use the No due date option so ABS can create the preferred delivery due date, generate a new schedule, and document that Yareli will call the clinic for the new delivery date.
Keywords: OCIN, two days short, 2 days short, not more than 5 days, 5 days or less, due date, delivery date, No due date, generate schedule, Yareli call clinic
Notes: Use this procedure only when the delivery date is not more than five days away AND ABS says the schedule will be short by two days. For a more-than-five-days due-date exception, follow KB-094.
Purpose: Provide the approved ABS due-date adjustment procedure when the delivery date is five days or less away and the generated schedule is two days short.
Step-by-Step Procedure:
1. Confirm that the delivery date is not more than five days away and that ABS indicates the schedule will be short by two days.
2. In ABS, go to the Due Date selection area.
3. Click the square "No due date" button.
4. Allow ABS to create the preferred delivery due date.
5. Click Generate to create the new schedule.
6. Add the following note in ABS: "Yareli to call for new delivery date of [enter the delivery date set by ABS]."
Stop / Escalate When: Do not use this procedure if the delivery date is more than five days away or if the schedule exception is different from two days short. Use the applicable scheduling SOP or escalate if the scenario is not covered.

Question: What are the Incisive tooth ranges and model-selection rules for Mini, Quadrant, and Full Arch?
Official Answer / SOP: For Incisive cases, do not enter Mini models. Use only Quadrant or Full Arch based on the tooth combination and Doctor Preferences. Anterior teeth are 6–11 and 22–27. Posterior teeth are 1–5, 12–16, 17–21, and 28–32. An anterior/incisor case uses Full Arch. If a two-tooth case combines anterior and posterior teeth, use Full Arch. If three posterior teeth are on opposing sides, use Full Arch. If two posterior teeth are on the same arch/next to each other, use Quadrant. The source guide also notes OCIN11553 as a Full-model account; account/doctor-specific preferences remain authoritative when they explicitly differ.
Keywords: Incisive, no mini, mini model, quadrant, quadrant arch, full arch, anterior teeth, posterior teeth, 6-11, 22-27, 1-5, 12-16, 17-21, 28-32, two posterior, three posterior, opposing side, OCIN11553
Notes: The supplied guide uses the wording “Full charge models” in one example; the surrounding guide and diagrams identify this as the Full Arch model selection. Doctor Preferences or an explicit account-specific rule override the general default when stated.
Source Basis: Uploaded Incisive model-selection guide with tooth diagrams
Purpose: Provide one authoritative Incisive model-selection reference for tooth ranges and common multi-tooth combinations.
Step-by-Step Procedure:
1. Confirm the case belongs to the Incisive workflow.
2. Check Doctor Preferences and any explicit account-specific model rule before applying a general default.
3. Do not select a Mini model for an Incisive case; use Quadrant or Full Arch.
4. Classify the teeth using the visual ranges: anterior = 6–11 and 22–27; posterior = 1–5, 12–16, 17–21, and 28–32.
5. If the case is anterior/incisor, select Full Arch.
6. If a two-tooth case combines an anterior tooth and a posterior tooth, select Full Arch.
7. If three posterior teeth are on opposing sides, select Full Arch.
8. If two posterior teeth are on the same arch/next to each other, select Quadrant.
9. Recheck the model selection against the Rx and Doctor Preferences before generating the schedule.
Stop / Escalate When: Stop and verify the rule if the tooth combination is not covered by the visual guide, if the case is not clearly Incisive, or if a Doctor Preference/account-specific instruction conflicts with the general rule.
Title: Incisive Model Selection & Tooth-Range Visual Guide
